content.overview: Any amendment of the articles shall be proposed by not less than two-thirds of the elected directors or by not less than one-third of the Members of the Producer Company, and adopted by the Members by a special resolution. A copy of the amended articles together with a copy of the special resolution, both duly certified by two directors, shall be filed with the Registrar within fifteen days from the date of its adoption.
content.glance: Articles may be amended only on the prescribed proposal threshold and special resolution; filing with the Registrar within 15 days is mandatory.
content.study: Section 378I sets a dual threshold for proposing an amendment of the articles (two-thirds of elected directors or one-third of Members) and requires adoption by special resolution. The amended articles and the special resolution must be certified by two directors and filed with the Registrar within fifteen days of adoption.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Amendment of articles requires proposal by ≥2/3 elected directors or ≥1/3 Members, adoption by special resolution, and filing with the Registrar within 15 days.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378I
examples.body: A proposal by two-thirds of the elected directors, followed by a special resolution of the Members and timely Registrar filing, validly amends the articles under s. 378I.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378I?
hypotheticals.analysis: It fixes the proposal threshold, the special-resolution requirement and the 15-day filing duty for amendment of the articles.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming ordinary Board majority is enough to propose an articles amendment.
misconceptions.correction: The proposal must come from at least two-thirds of the elected directors or one-third of the Members.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 378I be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Check proposal threshold. II. Confirm special resolution and filing. III. Conclude.
